readme.section: mega-index-map
readme.text:
A cross-workspace Library for DeepSeek Harness. Agents record the objects they meet - files, tools,
environments, knowledge, work records - into `$DSH_HOME/library`, so any conversation can index,
search and reuse them.

readme.section: mega-index-map
readme.text:
Every tool says when it is the cheaper answer, because that is what decides whether an agent asks the
Library or walks the filesystem: `library_query` before researching something again, `library_detect`
before looking for a tool or runtime, `library_sniff` before opening a file to guess its type, and
`library_index op=audit` before walking a directory to see what is in it. For a host that still reaches
for the disk, `injectPrompt: true` (plugin config) prepends a short notice to each session's first user
message - replace its wording wholesale with `$DSH_HOME/mega-index-prompt.md`.

readme.section: Tools
readme.text:
- `library_record` - record an object (change detection routes verify/confirm; a change to the immutable
  class is refused until the user decides, and is then recorded with `confirm: true` and a `reason`, which
  the log keeps as `record-confirm`)
- `library_index` - four jobs on the index: `op=rebuild` (default) dedupes/sorts and reports conflicts;
  `op=audit dir=<path>` reconciles a directory with the Library read-only, both directions - entries on
  disk with no record, and records whose path no longer exists (recorded is not the same as addressable);
  `op=index dir=<path> confirm=true` registers the missing entries, bounded by depth and an entry
  ceiling, with the sensitive-content rule applied (a file also gets a sha256 while we are standing on it).
  `op=verify` checks identity rather than existence: for every record that points at a regular file it
  recomputes the fingerprint and reports unchanged / changed / gone / never fingerprinted / unreadable -
  `gone` and `unreadable` stay separate findings, because a locked file is not a missing one. Read-only
  unless `confirm=true`, which also records the observed sha256 (how a baseline is established or
  refreshed); bounded

readme.section: First run: mine the history before claiming to be installed
readme.text:
On its first start the plugin reads every session it can find and mines what a Library actually indexes -
tools that resolve on this machine, paths that exist, local endpoints, environment variables that are set,
and file formats this library does not know yet. Everything else in a conversation is dropped: a
246-session store (measured: 523 MB compressed, 1,509 MB decompressed, 1,478,647 records, read in 70.8 s)
leaves verified facts rather than a transcript archive: measured here, 253 sessions and 1,484,547 records
yielded 11,253 rows in about 49 minutes.
A format lead has to be seen at least twice to be recorded at all: in 1.5 million records an extension
mentioned once is usually a hash or a token, while a format that matters recurs. Mined rows carry
`source: session-mining` with a name derived from the fact itself, so a later pass replaces them instead
of piling up.

readme.section: First run: mine the history before claiming to be installed
readme.text:
`bootstrap` decides how it runs: `blocking` (default - this Library registers its tools only after the
pass finishes), `gate` (it starts in the background and `op=status` reports it), or `off` (only an
explicit `op=bootstrap` runs it). `bootstrapBudgetMs` (default 300000) stops a pass cleanly, so a very
long history finishes over several starts instead of holding the host open, and it resumes where it
stopped. Every step is appended to `$DSH_HOME/library/bootstrap-progress.jsonl` with the current state in
`bootstrap-state.json` - one line per session, naming the file being read - so progress is visible while
it happens rather than only at the end.

readme.section: What a sensitive record can and cannot do
readme.text:
The sensitive-content rule is deliberate, and it is worth knowing exactly what it buys, because a record
about a *security tool* (a virus scanner, a signature rule set, a password vault, an encrypted-volume tool)
trips it for the plainest of reasons: the words that describe the domain are the words the patterns look
for. Such an object is stored encrypt-isolated, and it exposes only

```text
{ id, type, name, source, sensitive: true, createdAt, __content }
```

readme.section: What a sensitive record can and cannot do
readme.text:
Everything else - `path`, `description`, `summary`, `tags` - is inside the encrypted blob. Three
consequences follow, and none of them is a fault:

readme.section: What a sensitive record can and cannot do
readme.text:
- **It is findable by what it is called, not by what it says.** `library_query` can match the name and the
  source; a keyword that only appeared in its summary or tags will not find it.
- **`op=verify` skips it**, because its `path` lives in the blob and there is nothing to fingerprint. A
  report of `unchanged: 0` therefore does not cover sensitive records.
- **The body is one explicit step away**: `library_decrypt id=<id>` returns it, `library_export` keeps it
  encrypted on the way out, and every manual decrypt is written to the append-only log.

readme.section: What a sensitive record can and cannot do
readme.text:
Rewording a description to slip past the patterns is not a workaround this plugin offers: it would evade a
deliberate boundary to gain readability and leave the record vaguer than it started. The honest route is
`library_index op=review`: with an id, a decision (`clear` or `revoke`) and a reason it either makes one
encrypted body readable or puts the rule back - per object, never by name or pattern, always written to the
append-only log, and a cleared object carries the review that let it through. `op=review` with no id lists
every object that carries one. Use it for records **about software** (a scanner, a rule set, a password
vault: the words that describe the domain are the words the patterns look for), never for the material
itself - a sample, a key or a credential path stays encrypted.

readme.section: What a sensitive record can and cannot do
readme.text:
One more thing about samples, because it is easy to get backwards: **the Library seals references, never
material**. Encrypting a record about a quarantined sample hides *where the sample is and what it is
called*; it does not touch the file, which stays exactly where it is (this plugin only ever writes inside
`$DSH_HOME`). Software that learns from a corpus reads the corpus from disk, not from this index. What
makes that workable is keeping the two surrounding layers readable: the **directory records** that say
where a corpus lives, and the **tooling** that fetches, stores and scans it. Seal the individual items,
keep the anchors and the code visible, and a detector under development can still find everything it
needs - through the filesystem, which is where it was always going to read them from. The rule also
considers a record's `path` when deciding what is sensitive, so a sample named after its own hash is caught
by where it lives rather than by a word in its name.

readme.section: What a sensitive record can and cannot do
readme.text:
Changing that rule is worth checking rather than assuming, because a rule that can see a path (or any new
rule) can make records written long ago look sensitive in hindsight. `library_index op=review what=candidates`
is read-only: it lists the readable records the current patterns would seal, with the pattern that matched
each one. Run it after touching the patterns. It is how a rule meant to catch quarantined samples turned out
never to match anything, and how the records that predate the rule seeing a path were found - forty of them,
of which three were credential stores and thirty-seven were a toolchain that merely mentions credentials.

readme.section: What a sensitive record can and cannot do
readme.text:
The list has two halves, and both are read-only. `op=review what=candidates` answers what the current
patterns would seal among the records that are readable right now; `op=review what=sealed` answers the
converse - which encrypted records carry no review marker, meaning a pattern sealed them and nobody has
judged them. The second list is where the noise hides (a Windows component, an npm package that merely
mentions credentials, a login icon), and it is equally where a record that really *is* material should be
confirmed rather than assumed. Clearing a record takes it off that list and onto the review record; leaving
it alone is also a decision, and the list is what makes the difference visible.

readme.section: What changed in 0.4.3
readme.text:
- `library_project`'s hmoca/hmyr rule learns the second way this language loads a source: the import
  statement is a dependency edge exactly like `loadUnit("./x.hmoca")` is. Both spellings show up in
  `op=map` now.
- The js/ts rule learns two more shapes it used to miss.
- `op=affects` no longer fails its own output schema.
- The ASCII invariant is green again after an edit slipped a non-ASCII character into the text.

readme.section: What changed in 0.4.3
readme.text:
0.4.2 was the release that documented the map itself: `library_project` plus the "point the map at the
test that matters" habit.

readme.section: Notes
readme.text:
- The library lives at `$DSH_HOME/library` (default `~/.dsh/library`). Additions learned on this
  machine live beside it and never override the built-in tables.
- Work stays local: the plugin performs no network I/O and transmits nothing on its own.
- `library_index op=status` is the whole-library view in one read: object counts by type and source, how
  many records are encrypted and how many were cleared by a review, fingerprint coverage over the paths
  that can be fingerprinted, addresses versus paths, internal consistency (duplicate keys, missing fields,
  a sensitive flag without a blob), and the last disk-side findings quoted from the append-only log with
  their timestamps - so seeing the whole library never means walking the disk again.
- Measured cost at this machine's current scale - 11,649 objects, 6.0 MB index: a query takes about
  51 ms, recording one object 156 ms (it rewrites the index), a rebuild 124 ms (0 conflicts, 0 duplicates),
  and a status read 10 ms. At 5,000 objects the same three were 13 / 19 / 26 ms with a 2.3 MB index.
  Back up or migrate with `library_export`. Those figures have a guard rail now: `npm run bench` measures the

readme.section: mega-index-map
readme.text:
已签名的发布物带一份 PKCS#7 签名、一个哈希文件与公钥证书；怎么验证、以及签名证明了什么、没证明什么，都写在
[docs/verification.md](docs/verification.md)。
维护者那一侧写在 [docs/releasing.md](docs/releasing.md)：发布怎么切、推送之后 CI 会做什么。

> 英文原文：[README.md](README.md)

面向 DeepSeek Harness 的跨工作区资料库（Library）。Agent 把遇到的对象——文件、工具、环境、知识、
工作记录——记进 `$DSH_HOME/library`，任何会话都能索引、检索并复用它们。

readme.section: mega-index-map
readme.text:
每把工具的描述都写明了「什么时候它才是更省事的那条路」——因为这决定了 agent 是去问库，还是去
遍历文件系统：重新研究某个东西之前用 `library_query`，找工具或运行时之前用 `library_detect`，
打开文件猜类型之前用 `library_sniff`，手动翻目录看有什么之前用 `library_index op=audit`。如果宿主
仍然习惯性去扫盘，可开 `injectPrompt: true`（插件配置），它会把一段简短提示前置到每个会话的首条用户
消息；想换措辞就把文本写到 `$DSH_HOME/mega-index-prompt.md`，整体替换。

readme.section: 工具
readme.text:
- `library_record` - 记录一个对象（带变更检测，走 verify/confirm 判定；不可变类的变更会先被拒绝，等用户决定后再用 `confirm: true` 加 `reason` 记录，日志里留下 `record-confirm`）
- `library_index` - 索引上的四件事：`op=rebuild`（默认）去重排序并报告冲突；`op=audit dir=<路径>` 只读地把
  某目录与资料库对账，**双向**——磁盘上有、库里没记的条目，以及库里记着、路径已不存在的记录（「记过」不等于
  「还找得到」）；`op=index dir=<路径> confirm=true` 把缺的条目登记成记录，受深度与条目上限约束，并照样套用
  敏感内容规则（顺手给文件算一次 sha256）。
  `op=verify` 查的是**同一性**而不是存在性：凡是记录指向普通文件的，重算指纹并报出
  **未变 / 已变 / 已消失 / 从未取过指纹 / 读不了**——「消失」与「读不了」分开算，被锁住的文件不是失踪文件。
  默认只读，`confirm=true` 才把观测到的 sha256 写回（这就是建立或刷新基线的方式）；受 `maxFiles` 与时间预算
  约束，用 `after=<id>` 作游标，大库可以切片走。超过 `maxHashBytes`（默认 16 MiB）的文件按「大小＋首尾各一段」
  取指纹，并如实标 `partial: true`，不冒充完整摘要。
  `op=prune confirm=true` 删掉不再符合条件的派生行——被提及次数少于 `keepHits` 的格式线索——所以以后
  收紧规则也能作用于已经记下的内容。**盘根会被拒绝**：会自顾自走遍整块盘的索引器，正是这个库要替代的那种扫描
- `library_query` - 按关键词、类型、标签检索，游标分页。多词查询按词逐个匹配、并按每个对象覆盖了几个词排序，所以多写几个词是**收窄**结果而不是要求那串字连续出现；单个词仍是普通的子串匹配。
- `library_detect` - 扫描并登记本机的工具与环境。内置清单与具体机器无关：裸命令名从 `PATH` 解析，位置一律
  用它的所有者自己的说法来写（`%ProgramFiles%`、`%GOROOT%`、`%ANDROID_HOME%`、`~`、`${HOME}`），会随版本
  变动的目录则从磁盘上取「最新安装的那个」。放在自选位置的工具用 `add` 写进本机候选包，`propose` 可以从某个
  目录推荐条目；不存在的路径会被跳过。每条已存在的结果还带 `declared`：文件自己对自己的声明（产品名／版本／
  厂商，来自它自己的版本资源，纯静态读取——绝不执

readme.section: 首次运行：先把历史淘一遍，再自称装好
readme.text:
插件第一次启动时会读遍能找到的所有会话，从中**只**淘出资料库真正要索引的东西——本机真实存在的工具、
真实存在的路径、本地端点、已设置的环境变量，以及这个格式库还不认识的文件格式；对话里的其余内容一概丢弃。
本机实测：253 个会话、1,484,547 条记录，淘出来的是**经过存在性验证**的 11,253 条事实（约 49 分钟），
而不是一座转写仓库。
格式线索要**至少被提及两次**才会入库：在一百五十万条记录里只出现一次的扩展名，通常是个哈希或词元；
真正要紧的格式会反复出现。淘洗记录统一带 `source: session-mining`、名字由事实本身决定，
所以再跑一遍是**覆盖**而不是堆积。

readme.section: 首次运行：先把历史淘一遍，再自称装好
readme.text:
`bootstrap` 决定它怎么跑：`blocking`（默认——淘洗完才注册本库的工具）、`gate`（后台开跑，`op=status` 汇报
进度）、`off`（只有显式 `op=bootstrap` 才跑）。`bootstrapBudgetMs`（默认 300000）让一趟干净停下，超长历史
分几次启动跑完，并且**从断点续跑**。每一步都会追加到 `$DSH_HOME/library/bootstrap-progress.jsonl`，当前状态
在 `bootstrap-state.json`——每会话一行、写明正在读哪个文件，所以进度是当场可见，而不是只在结尾给个总数。

readme.section: 敏感记录能做什么、不能做什么
readme.text:
敏感内容判定是**有意**的，而它买到了什么值得写清楚——因为一条关于**安全工具**的记录（杀毒引擎、签名规则
集、密码库、加密卷工具）会以最朴素的方式命中它：描述这个领域用的词，正是词表要找的词。这类对象以加密隔离
存储，只暴露：

```text
{ id, type, name, source, sensitive: true, createdAt, __content }
```

其余一切——`path`、`description`、`summary`、`tags`——都在密文里。由此有三个后果，**它们都不是故障**：

readme.section: 敏感记录能做什么、不能做什么
readme.text:
- **它靠"叫什么"可被找到，而不是靠"说了什么"**：`library_query` 能匹配名称与 source；只出现在 summary
  或 tags 里的关键词是搜不到它的。
- **`op=verify` 会跳过它**：它的 `path` 在密文里，没有可校验的指纹。所以一份报 `unchanged: 0` 的报告
  **不覆盖**敏感记录。
- **正文只差一次显式动作**：`library_decrypt id=<id>` 取回它，`library_export` 导出时仍保持加密，而每一次
  手工解密都会写进追加日志。

readme.section: 敏感记录能做什么、不能做什么
readme.text:
**改写描述去绕过词表，不是本插件提供的变通**：那是为了可读性去规避一道有意的边界，并且让记录比原来更含糊。
正路是 **`library_index op=review`**：给 `id`、`decision`（`clear`／`revoke`）与 `reason`，它要么把**一条**加密正文变成可读、要么把规则放回去——**逐条**、绝不按名字或模式、每次都写进追加日志，而且被放行的对象身上**带着**这次
复核（谁在何时为了什么放行）。不带 `id` 调用则列出**所有**带复核标记的对象。它用于**关于软件**的记录（扫描器、
规则集、密码库——描述这个领域的词正是词表要找的词），**绝不**用于**材料本身**：样本、密钥、凭据路径照旧加密。

readme.section: 敏感记录能做什么、不能做什么
readme.text:
关于样本还有一件容易被弄反的事：**库封的是「引用」，不是「材料」**。把一条隔离区样本的记录加密，藏起来的是
*它叫什么、在哪*；文件本身一动不动（这个插件只写 `$DSH_HOME` 之内）。**要学语料的软件从磁盘读语料，不经过这个
索引**。让这条能成立的关键，是把**外面两层保持可读**：说明「语料在哪」的**目录记录**，以及负责抓取、存放、扫描
的**工具脚本**。**封住单件，保留锚点与代码**，开发中的检测器照样能找到它需要的一切——经由文件系统，而那本来就是
它读的地方。另外，判定敏感时会**把 `path` 一起看**：一个以自身哈希命名的样本，是靠「它放在哪里」被抓到的，
而不是靠名字里有没有某个词。

readme.section: 敏感记录能做什么、不能做什么
readme.text:
改了规则就该**核对**而不是假设——因为一条能看见路径的规则（或任何新规则），都会让很久以前写下的记录在事后显得敏感。
`library_index op=review what=candidates` 是**只读**的：列出**按现行词表会被密封**的可读记录，并写明**命中的是哪条模式**。
改完词表就跑一次。这条能力正是靠它自己发现的：一条本该抓隔离区样本的规则其实**从未匹配过任何东西**，以及那些**早于
"规则能看见路径"**的记录有 40 条——其中 3 条是凭据存储，37 条只是"提到凭据"的工具链。

readme.section: 敏感记录能做什么、不能做什么
readme.text:
这份清单有两半，都只读。`op=review what=candidates` 回答的是「按现行词表，**当前可读**的记录里哪些会被封」；
`op=review what=sealed` 回答的是反面——**哪些加密记录没有复核标记**，也就是「被词表自动封住、但没有任何人判断过」。
后一份清单既是噪声藏身之处（Windows 组件、只是名字里带凭据的 npm 包、登录图标），也正是**真材料应当被确认而不是被假设**的
地方。放行一条就把它从这份清单移到复核记录里；什么都不做**也是一个决定**——而这份清单让这个区别变得可见。

readme.section: 0.4.3 改了什么
readme.text:
- `library_project` 的 hmoca/hmyr 规则学会这门语言装载源码的第二种写法：`引入 "./x.hmoca"` 与
  `loadUnit("./x.hmoca")` 一样，都是图上的一条边。两种写法现在都会出现在 `op=map` 里。
- js/ts 规则补上两种它以前漏掉的形状。
- `op=affects` 不再违反它自己的输出 schema。
- 一处编辑混进了非 ASCII 字符之后，ASCII 不变式恢复为通过。

0.4.2 是把地图本身写进文档的那一版：`library_project`，以及「把地图指向真正相关的那一个测试」这条习惯。

readme.section: 说明
readme.text:
- 资料库位于 `$DSH_HOME/library`（默认 `~/.dsh/library`）。本机学到的扩充条目与它同处一地，
  **永不覆盖**内置表。
- 一切留在本机：插件不做任何网络 I/O，也不会自行外发任何内容。
- `library_index op=status` 是**一次读取看全局**：按类型与来源的对象计数、多少条记录被加密、多少条经复核放行、
  可指纹路径上的指纹覆盖率、地址与路径各多少、内部一致性（重复键、缺字段、标了敏感却没有密文），以及**从追加日志里
  引用的上一次磁盘侧结论**（带时间）——所以看全局永远不需要再走一遍磁盘。
- 实测开销随规模线性增长且很小：本机当前规模（11,649 个对象、索引 6.0 MB）下，查询约 51 ms、记一条
  156 ms（会重写索引）、重建 124 ms（0 冲突、0 重复）、读一次状态 10 ms；5,000 个对象时这三项分别是
  13 / 19 / 26 ms（索引 2.3 MB）。备份与迁移用 `library_export`。这些数字现在有护栏了：`npm run bench` 用一次性临时库测同样四项操作，
  `npm run bench:check` 与提交在仓库里的基线比对，**故意把容忍倍数放得很宽**（这台机器是共享的，要抓的是
  **数量级**变化而不是计时噪声）。它**不放进 `npm run check`**——把计时测量塞进不变量链，只会让不变量又慢又不稳。
- 并发写入经锁文件串行化：持有者已死的锁会被接管；锁正忙时最多等两秒，之后照写并在日志里说明。
- 本包与同源的另一版本（跨 harness 版）**互不写入**：本包只写 `$DSH_HOME`、系统临时目录，或调用方
  显式给出的路径；`scripts/check-isolation.mjs` 对两个方向都强制（详见 [ISOLATION.md](ISOLATION.md)）。
- 三条不变量每次推送都检查：**英文/ASCII 输出**、**Windows/macOS/Linux 可移植**、**多语言文本的
  UTF-8 安全**。`npm run check` 跑全部四项检查（ASCII、一致性、可移植性、隔离）；`npm run selfcheck`
  跑五段自检——测通、遍历、校对、遍历、测通——并按轴分别报告。
- 本文件是仓库里唯一的本地化文档（也是 ASCII 不变量唯一的散文类例外），其余文本与代码仍为纯 ASCII。
